message: reads the tag at offset 666 (`<span class="pct-pair__count" [it's]="count()">{count(), plural, =0 {it's none here} other {<span class="pct-pair__more"`) on into the ICU at offset 713 — a `<` in an expression, a string or a text opens a tag to the scan that ends past the ICU's start, and so does a real tag holding a quote Angular reads as part of a bracketed name (`[it's]`) where the scan, pairing each quote with the next of its kind, meets its first `>` outside them past that start; what the ICU's cases draw
$reason: `icu-behind-a-false-tag` with a real tag in the false one's place: the count's `<span>` holds a bracketed name with a quote, `[it's]`, and the ICU inside it an apostrophe in its first case, `it's none here`. Angular's lexer reads the name up to its closing bracket, and the template parses; the tag scan pairs the name's quote with the case's apostrophe, and the count's tag runs on past the ICU's start to the `>` of the stop the second case draws. The scan's reading running into the ICU refused it before this case too. What the case holds is the refusal's word for why: it named a `<` in an expression, a string or a text alone, and the tag that runs into the ICU here is the count's own.
